FOREWORD after the draft finalized by the This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, Organic Chemicals ( Miscellaneous ) Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. Sodium formate ( sodium salt of formic acid ) is used as a tanning agent in leather industry, in the manufacture of various chemicals like formic acid, sodium hydrosulphite, various metal formates, in dyeing and printing fabrics and also in analytical chemistry as a precipitant for the noble metals. It is manufactured a) by direct on industrial synthesis scale, generally reaction by two routes sodium : hydroxide and carbon monoxide; and

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of` a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in ;Lccordance with IS 2 : 1960 <Rules for rounding bfl' uumcrical values ( reui.red )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

The colour produced and extracted in mixed solvent's layer, when the material is treated with and potassium thiocyanate hydrochloric acid followed by mixture of amyl alcohol and any1 acetate, is compared to that produced by the standard iron solution under identical conditions. Weigh accurately about 5 g of sample (~$1) and dissolve it in 50 ml of wa.ter. Add 10 ml of hydrochloric acid and boil it until the total volume is reduced to about 10 ml. Cool and transfer into IOO-ml volumetric flask and make up to the mark with distilled water. Take 10 ml of made up solution in a Nessler tube. Add few drops of 0.2 N potassium permanganate solution till permanganate colour persists and add 5 ml of 20 percent potassium thiocyanate solution, shake well, add 10 ml of amy 1 alcohol, amyl acetate mixture and extract the roloured iron complex in this mixtures layer. Carry out a blank test by taking 1 ml of hydrochloric acid in another Nessler cylinder and add these reagents in the same order. Then add standard iron solution drop by drop to the blank Nessler tube until both the tubes have same intensity of colour observed in an organic layer. Note the volume of standard iron solution consumed (V) for producing the colour ( cqu~l to that of sample ) in the blank tube. E-4 CALCULATION Iron, where ppm = vx M 10

E-2.5

Standard Iron Solution

Dissolve 7.022 g of ferrous ammonium sulphate in a mixture of 600 ml of water and 350 ml of dilute sulphuric acid and dilute to 1 000 ml with water. Further dilute 1 ml of the solution so obtained to 1 000 ml with water. One millilitre of the diluted solution contains 0.001 mg of iron ( as Fe ).

J-l.3 precautions shall be taken to protect the silmples, the material being sampled, the sampling instrument and the containers for samples 11om adventitious contamination. J-l.4 To draw a representative sample, the contents of each container selected for sampling shall be mixed as thoroughly as possible by suitable means.

J-l.7 Each sample container shall bc sealed airtight after filling and marked with full idcntification particulars such as sample number, the date: of sampling, batch of manufacture of the material and other important particulars of the consignmcht. 6

iS 13475: 1992 J-2 Scale of Sampling J-2.1 Lot
In a single consignment, all packages of the same sizes, containing material from the same batch of manufacture, shall constitute a lot. If a consignment is known to consist cf packages belonging to different batches of manufacture, packages belonging to the same batch of manufacture shall be grouped together and each such group shall constitute a lot. J-2.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the material in a lot to the requirements of this specification, samples shall be tested on each lot separately. J-2.3 `Ihe rnmber of Fackages to be sampled for this Furpose shall depend on the size of the~lot and shzll be in actor_dance with Table 2.

J-3 PREPARATION

OF SAMPLES

J-3.1 From each of the

packages selected, draw with an appropriate sampling instrument small quantity of material from different portions of the packages and mix thoroughly. This shall constitute the representative sample for the package. J-3.2 From the sample representing different packages selected in J-2.3 small but approximately equal quantity of material shall be taken and mixed thoroughly to form a composite sample which shall be sufficient for carrying out triplicate tests for the characteristics given in Table 1. The composite sample shall be divided into three equal another for the parts, one for the purchaser, supplier and third for the reference.

Table 2 Scale of Sampling
Lot Size Number of Containers to be Selected (2) 3 4 5 6

J-3.3 The referee sample shall bear the seals of both the purchaser and the supplier and shall be kept at a place agreed to between the two. It shall be used in case of any dispute between the two. J-3.4 The composite sample shall be transferred to separate containers. The sample containers shall then be sealed with stoppers and labeled full identification particulars given with in J-1.7.

CRITERIA

FOR CONFORMlTY

The lot shall be declared as conforming to this specification, if the test results on ,the composite sample for each of the characteristics meet relevant requirements given in Table 1.

Standard Mark
The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by B1S and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are ah.0 continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
